events.title: iMac G3 released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iMac G3 on August 15, 1998 — an all-in-one Mac with USB, no floppy drive, and translucent "Bondi Blue" design.
events.about: The iMac made USB mainstream and gave web designers and developers a stylish Unix-based desktop with Mac OS 8. It sold millions, reviving Apple before the iPod and iPhone. The all-in-one form factor and emphasis on internet out-of-the-box aligned with the late-1990s web boom.

narrative.whyChosen: The iMac G3 saved Apple commercially and pushed USB as the standard peripheral connector.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought millions of new users — and developers — back to the Mac platform.
narrative.problemSolved: Consumers wanted a simple, internet-ready computer without legacy ports and beige boxes.
